question: Should generic tool-progress intent be a supported public Plugin SDK reply-payload contract?
rationale: Direct Codex inspection supports the transient-versus-terminal distinction, but exposing that distinction to third-party plugins is a long-term API choice that functional review cannot settle.

options.title: Approve the narrow public contract
options.body: Retain the marker and predicate after the Slack native-block defect is fixed and accept them as portable reply-payload presentation metadata.

options.title: Keep the signal internal
options.body: Remove the public exports and carry equivalent progress intent through a bundled runtime-only seam.

recommendation.title: Approve the narrow public contract
recommendation.body: Retain the marker and predicate after the Slack native-block defect is fixed and accept them as portable reply-payload presentation metadata.

likelyOwner.reason: The broad history signal spans the affected Slack, Codex, and public Plugin SDK paths, making this the best available owner for the cross-boundary API choice.
